On October 1, 2026, the on-demand price of H100 on Nebius rose from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU hour. This is a 16.9% increase for a Hopper family GPU.

The gap between vendors is much bigger than the increase. The listed on-demand price for H100 ranges between $3.99 per GPU hour on Lambda and $12.29 on Azure.

AWS is next on October 7. The reserved price of H100 in AWS Capacity Block increased by 15% to $5.970 per GPU hour.

- Nebius increased its rate for its H100 on-demand to 16.9% on October 1 from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour. Its preemptible price remains at $2.15.
- On-demand H100 prices currently range from $3.99 (Lambda) to $12.29 (Azure) per GPU-hour.

- The price differs depending on the region, GPU configuration, and purchase type, so do a like-to-like comparison.
- Outdated figures include $2.99 for Lambda and $98.32 for AWS p5.48xlarge.

## What changed on October 1

As of October 1, 2026, Nebius revised the pricing of compute for four GPUs. You can find the old and new pricing in Nebius’s documentation.

They have not adjusted the preemptible pricing. Therefore, the H100 preemptible price remains at $2.15. This widens the gap with the on-demand option.

## What the Nebius increase does and doesn’t tell us

Nebius has not published a reason in the documentation we reviewed. Toobit’s report on the notice reads the increase as a sign that scarce capacity still carries pricing power.

One increase at one provider does not set the market. AWS cut H100 on-demand prices by 44% in June 2025, per Data Centre Dynamics. CoreWeave’s H100 node price did not change in our check.

results.title: Nebius raises prices across the board on… · Slicast
highlights:
# Nebius raises prices across the board on October 1: H100 +17% to $4.50/hour, B300 to $9.50/hour

Trade press Slicast · October 6, 2026 at 21:09 UTC · Global · Source: Shattered.io

importance 78

N ebius, the Amsterdam-based neocloud provider, notified customers on September 17, 2026 that it will raise pay-as-you-go prices for Nvidia GPU instances, AMD CPU capacity, and memory starting October 1, 2026. It's the company's second price hike in three months, and this time the increases stretch well beyond GPUs into the CPU and memory tiers that most cloud budgets treat as an afterthought.

The numbers are specific. Nvidia H100 instances rise roughly 17% to $4.50 per GPU-hour from $3.85, H200 climbs 20% to $5.40 from $4.50, B200 goes up about 19% to $8.50 from $7.15, and the newest B300 chips take the biggest hit at 21%, reaching $9.50 per GPU-hour from $7.85. AMD EPYC Genoa CPU rates jump 25%, and memory pricing rises about 41%, the steepest increase across the board. Investors read it as a sign of tight capacity, not weak demand: Nebius shares (Nasdaq: NBIS) jumped as much as 11.1% in pre-market trading the same day.

For a team running a sustained H100 workload, that 17% translates to an extra $0.65 per GPU-hour, which compounds fast across a multi-GPU training cluster running around the clock. What stands out is the memory line. A 41% jump on memory-backed capacity is the largest single increase Nebius applied, bigger than any of the GPU tiers. Memory rarely makes cloud pricing headlines because it's usually bundled into instance pricing rather than billed separately, but Nebius broke it out this time, which suggests memory availability, not just GPU silicon, is now a binding constraint on how much compute the company can actually deliver.

This is not an isolated move. Around May 2026, Nebius already raised on-demand capacity prices by an average of 29% and spot capacity by 51%. That means Nebius has now raised prices twice in under half a year, with the spring spot-market increase actually exceeding the September GPU hikes in percentage terms. Reuters framed the September move plainly: Nebius is raising prices because demand for computing power keeps rising faster than supply. It's closer to basic capacity rationing, the same mechanism that pushed cloud GPU rental rates up during the original 2023 H100 shortage, except this time it's spreading into CPU and memory tiers that used to be treated as commodity add-ons.

...

Cloud GPU pricing is notoriously hard to compare directly because providers mix spot, on-demand, reserved, and multi-year contract rates on the same public price list. But looking at H100 rental rates across the market as of September 2026 shows just how wide the spread is. RunPod offers H100 instances at $1.99–$2.99 per GPU-hour on demand and marketplace rates, Lambda at $3.29–$3.99 on-demand. Nebius now sits at $4.50 from October 1, CoreWeave at $4.25–$6.16 on-demand, and AWS's P5 instance pricing approaches $6.88 per GPU on a list-price basis. Nebius's increase moves it higher on the ladder but still below legacy hyperscalers, maintaining its position as a specialist provider with more capacity allocation and tighter pricing than the market leaders.

results.title: GPU-Preiserhöhung von bis zu 21 % und Inferize-Übernahme:
highlights:
Wer GPU-Kapazität bei Nebius bucht, zahlt seit dem 1. Oktober mehr: H100-, H200-, B200- und B300-Instanzen wurden um 17 bis 21 % teurer, CPU-Tarife sogar um rund 25 %. Preiserhöhungen in dieser Größenordnung sind kein Routineschritt — sie setzen voraus, dass die Nachfrage die verfügbare Kapazität übersteigt oder zumindest nah daran ist.

Dazu passt die Übernahme von Inferize, einem Unternehmen, dessen Technologie die GPU-Auslastung in Nebius’ sogenannter „Token Factory”-Infrastruktur verbessern soll. Höhere Auslastung bei gleichzeitig gestiegenen Preisen wäre für die Einheitenökonomie eines kapitalintensiven AI-Cloud-Anbieters tatsächlich relevant — sofern die Nachfrage stabil bleibt.

...

Strategisch wird auch die Partnerschaft mit Palantir genannt, bei der Nebius als Infrastrukturpartner für souveräne und regulierte AI-Anwendungen fungiert. Gartner schätzt, dass Neocloud-Anbieter bis 2030 rund 20 % eines 267-Milliarden-Dollar-Marktes erreichen könnten — ein Rahmen, der Nebius-Bullen als Orientierung dient.

...

Die GPU-Tarife stiegen um 17 bis 21 %, CPU-Preise sogar um 25 %. Solche Schritte setzt nur durch, wer Nachfragedruck spürt — für uns ein glaubwürdiges operatives Signal. Gleichzeitig streut die Analystenmeinung extrem: 84 Dollar (Rothschild) gegen 399 Dollar (BNP Paribas). Der November-Bericht wird zeigen, ob die Auslastung die Margen tatsächlich bewegt — oder ob der EPS-Konsens von minus 0,53 Dollar die ehrlichere Zahl ist.

results.title: The lowest published H100 price across the nine providers we track changed hands this week, and it went up. Crusoe listed $3.90 per GPU-hour on September 27 and was not the lowest … | Bobby Clay
highlights:
The lowest published H100 price across the nine providers we track changed hands this week, and it went up. Crusoe listed $3.90 per GPU-hour on September 27 and was not the lowest of those nine. Crusoe listed $3.90 on October 4 and was. It never moved its price. Nebius raised past it, so the floor rose five cents and a different company now sets it.

Underneath the published side, the Ornn Compute Price Index, a third-party index of traded prices rather than quoted or listed ones, read A100 80 GB SXM4 at $0.88 on October 4, the lowest weekly reading we have recorded since tracking began on May 18.

H200 is the one you should examine. No provider changed an H200 price this week, and the distance between the lowest published rate across those nine and the traded index still more than doubled, from $0.55 on September 28 to $1.28. Watching list prices alone would have shown you nothing. If you picked a provider on price, the number is not what changed. The name under it is.

GPU cloud pricing updates monthly and sometimes weekly; marketplace platforms like Vast.ai can change hourly. The rates above were verified in September 2026 – re-check primary pricing pages before you deploy anything.

...

### On-demand

On-demand gives you immediate access at a fixed rate with no commitment. You pay for the whole time the instance (your running virtual server) is running, whether the GPU is processing a job or sitting idle. It’s the default model for variable or short-term workloads and the basis for every rate in the comparison table.

...

### H100 pricing per hour

An H100 costs $2.89 per hour on RunPod and up to $12.29 on Azure, as of September 2026. That is a more than 4x spread between the cheapest specialist cloud and the most expensive hyperscaler for the same chip. Hostinger doesn’t offer an H100; the B200 covers its top tier.

- RunPod:$2.89 (PCIe); $3.29 (SXM); $3.19 (NVL).
- Lambda:$3.29 (PCIe); from $3.99 (SXM; cheapest per-GPU at the 8-GPU config, single GPU available at $4.29).
- Nebius:$3.85.
- DigitalOcean:$4.41.
- AWS p5.4xlarge:$6.88 (single H100 SXM5; no minimum node).
- Azure NC H100 v5:$6.98 (NVL form factor, single GPU).
- GCP A3 (a3-highgpu-8g): from $11.06 per GPU (8-GPU minimum on-demand).
- Azure ND H100 v5:$12.29 per GPU ($98.32 for the 8-GPU node).

...

### B200 and H200 pricing

The B200 costs $4.50 per hour on Hostinger, $6.79 on RunPod, from $4.38 on Vast.ai, and from $6.69 on Lambda. The H200 starts at $3.87 on Vast.ai and $4.59 on RunPod. GCP’s A4 series starts around $16.11 per GPU-hour but requires a reservation. There’s no standard on-demand option.

The H200 (141 GB HBM3e, a high-bandwidth memory type) carries roughly 75% more VRAM than the H100; RunPod lists it at $4.59. GCP’s A3 Ultra and Azure’s ND H200 v5 also require reservations and aren’t available on standard on-demand.

Both cards sit above the H100, but in different ways: the B200 is a new architecture with higher throughput, while the H200 keeps the H100’s compute and adds memory. As these cards become more widely available, H100 on-demand rates are likely to keep falling. A100 pricing has already dropped below $1 per hour on some marketplace providers as the market shifts toward newer GPU generations.

results.title: NVIDIA B200: Specs, Price per GPU-Hour, and B200 vs H200 (2026)
highlights:
The NVIDIA B200 carries 180 GB of HBM3e at 8 TB/s per GPU and 9 PFLOPS of dense FP4. It rents for $5.98 to $7.99 per GPU-hour on RunPod, Modal, and Lambda in October 2026, about $150 a day, against $4.54 to $5.29 for an H200. Specs, cloud prices, B200 vs H200 vs H100, and GB200 NVL72.

...

The NVIDIA B200 is a Blackwell data center GPU with 180 GB of HBM3e at 8 TB/s per GPU, fifth-generation NVLink at 1.8 TB/s, and hardware FP4. An eight-GPU DGX B200 holds 1,440 GB of GPU memory and delivers 72 PFLOPS of dense FP4. Renting one B200 costs $5.98 to $7.99 per GPU-hour on October 24, 2026 (RunPod, Modal, Lambda), about 1.4x an H200, and NVIDIA publishes no list price for a single card. Per TB/s of memory bandwidth, the number that sets LLM decode speed, the B200 rents for less than the H200 or H100.

...

## NVIDIA B200 Price: Cloud Rental per GPU-Hour (October 2026)

These are the published on-demand prices for one B200, read from each provider's pricing page on October 24, 2026. Modal bills per second and charges CPU and RAM separately; RunPod and Lambda bundle host CPU, RAM, and disk into the hourly rate. Since our October 6 read, RunPod raised its Secure Cloud B200 from $6.79 to $7.99 and Lambda cut its 8x instance from $6.79 to $6.69.

B200 price per GPU-hour by provider (October 24, 2026)

| Provider | Plan | Price per GPU-hour | What is included |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Modal | Serverless, per second ($0.001736/s) | $6.25 | GPU only |
| RunPod | Community Cloud B200 pod, 180 GB | $5.98 | 180 GB VRAM, community-hosted |
| RunPod | Secure Cloud B200 pod, 180 GB | $7.99 | 28 vCPU, 283 GB RAM |
| Lambda | 8x B200 SXM6 instance | $6.69 | 208 vCPU, 2,900 GiB RAM, 22 TiB SSD |
| Lambda | 4x B200 SXM6 instance | $6.79 | 104 vCPU, 1,440 GiB RAM, 11 TiB SSD |
| Lambda | 1-Click Cluster, 2 weeks to 1 year | $8.87 (256+ GPUs) to $9.86 (16 GPUs) | InfiniBand cluster |
| Morph | Dedicated inference endpoint | $9.98 | Served model, OpenAI-compatible API |

To buy, NVIDIA does not list a price for a single B200. Northflank reported OEM quotes of $45,000 to $50,000 per GPU and complete 8x B200 servers above $500,000 in August 2025. At Lambda's $6.69 per hour, $45,000 buys about 6,700 GPU-hours of rental, or nine months of one GPU running around the clock, before power, cooling, and the host server. Running one B200 all day costs $150 on Modal and $192 on RunPod Secure Cloud.

## B200 vs H200 vs H100

The H200 and H100 share Hopper compute and differ in memory. The B200 moves to Blackwell, adds FP4, and raises memory and bandwidth again. For more on the Hopper pair, see H100 vs H200 and the NVIDIA H200 guide.

B200 vs H200 vs H100 (SXM, per GPU)

| Architecture | Blackwell | Hopper | Hopper |
| Memory | 180 GB HBM3e | 141 GB HBM3e | 80 GB HBM3 |
| Bandwidth | 8 TB/s | 4.8 TB/s | 3.35 TB/s |
| FP8 (sparse) | 9 PFLOPS | 3.96 PFLOPS | 3.96 PFLOPS |
| FP4 in hardware | Yes | No | No |
| NVLink per GPU | 1.8 TB/s | 900 GB/s | 900 GB/s |
| Rent (Oct 24, 2026) | $5.98 to $7.99 | $4.54 to $5.29 | $3.95 to $4.09 |

H200 rental prices are Modal ($0.001261/s) and RunPod Secure Cloud ($5.29). H100 prices are Modal ($0.001097/s) and Lambda's 8x and 4x instances ($3.99 and $4.09). The H200 price table lists six providers.
